resolutions.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2028 is the operation-start of the MGS III (Master Gas System phase 3) expansion. JPT/SPE states the program will 'raise the Kingdom's total capacity by an additional 3.15 Bcf/D by 2028 by installing 4000 km of pipelines'; BlackRidge project profile gives scheduled completion Q4 2028. Two independent sources support 2028. Contradiction to flag: individual EPC packages complete earlier — e.g. OGJ reports Sinopec packages 6/7 mechanical completion by May 31, 2027 — so 2028 is the overall program/network operation date, not every segment. Replaces the original DEAD_LINK aramco.com ref (timed out on verify).

StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea=Saudi Arabia. JPT/SPE describes the MGS as 'an extensive network of pipelines connecting Saudi Arabia's key gas production and processing sites' delivering to the domestic market; World Oil confirms the MGS-3 EPC packages laying pipelines across the Kingdom. OGJ separately notes Sinopec's scope is 'in-country' Saudi Arabia. Both endpoints are domestic (segment STS-2-STS-1 'EWJZG-1'); no cross-border component. Two independent sources.

Owner1=Aramco 100%. OGJ: 'Saudi Arabian Oil Co. (Aramco) has awarded Sinopec... a turn-key fixed-price contract' for the MGS-3 pipelines; JPT confirms Aramco owns and is executing the MGS network expansion. The MGS is Aramco's wholly owned domestic gas transmission network; contractors (Sinopec, L&T, etc.) are EPC builders, not owners. Two independent sources support Aramco 100% ownership. Replaces the original DEAD_LINK aramco.com + meed refs (aramco.com timed out; original meed slug not re-checked).
